bad.title: Reliance on AI-to-AI Validation Rather Than Independent Verification
bad.description: Your verification approach often involves comparing AI outputs against each other or asking AI to check its own work, rather than positioning yourself as the primary validator who cross-references against original sources. This can create an echo chamber where errors persist because all validation flows through AI systems rather than your independent judgment grounded in source materials.

bad.title: Surface-Level Analysis Without Exploring Root Causes
bad.description: You tend to identify what is wrong or missing without investigating why problems occur or what underlying principles would prevent them. Your analyses focus on observable symptoms—like missing timestamps or incomplete elements—rather than exploring the design factors, conceptual gaps, or structural issues that create these problems in the first place.

bad.title: Inconsistent Application of Testing and Refinement Practices
bad.description: Your engagement with iterative testing varies significantly across tasks—sometimes you conduct multiple refinement cycles and systematic testing, while other times you may skip testing entirely or not capture learnings from one iteration to inform the next. This inconsistency means you're not yet building testing into your automatic workflow, which limits your ability to reliably produce high-quality collaborative outcomes.

good.title: Commitment to Verification and Quality Control
good.description: You consistently recognize that AI outputs require validation and take active steps to check their quality. Whether comparing multiple translations, identifying errors in meeting summaries, or noting missing elements in operationalized plans, you refuse to accept AI responses at face value. This fundamental skepticism is essential for effective AI collaboration and provides a strong foundation for building more sophisticated verification skills.

good.title: Practical Gap Identification
good.description: You have a keen eye for noticing concrete, functional problems in AI outputs—missing actionable steps, incomplete coverage, or structural gaps. This attention to practical details means you can quickly spot when deliverables fall short of requirements and translate those observations into specific correction requests, making your feedback actionable and results-oriented.

good.title: Willingness to Explore Complexity
good.description: When faced with ambiguous or challenging situations, you demonstrate genuine curiosity and persistence in digging deeper. You ask follow-up questions, consider multiple interpretations, and show openness to discovering that problems are more nuanced than they first appear. This exploratory mindset is valuable for uncovering insights that surface-level analysis would miss.

overall.overview: Throughout this assessment, you demonstrated **solid foundational collaboration skills** with a particular strength in recognizing the need to verify AI outputs and spot concrete quality gaps. Your approach shows **good practical instincts for identifying when something is missing or incomplete**, and you actively engage with AI to request corrections when issues surface. The primary growth opportunity lies in **deepening your analytical approach**—moving from surface-level observation to exploring underlying principles, developing independent verification methods, and building more systematic testing habits that carry across different types of tasks.

improvements.title: Develop Independent Source-Based Verification Methods
improvements.description: Build verification habits that position you as the authoritative validator. When checking AI outputs, always go back to original source materials yourself rather than asking AI to self-check or comparing AI outputs to each other. Create a mental checklist: What does the source actually say? Does this output accurately reflect that? Where exactly is the evidence? This discipline will dramatically improve your ability to catch subtle errors and build justified confidence in your conclusions.

improvements.title: Ask "Why" to Move From Symptoms to Root Causes
improvements.description: When you identify a gap or error, push yourself one level deeper by exploring what caused it. If actionable steps are missing, ask: What would the prompt need to include for those steps to appear? If citations are vague, consider: What makes a citation precise versus generic? This root-cause thinking will help you design better instructions upfront and develop more sophisticated analytical frameworks that prevent problems rather than just catching them.

improvements.title: Build Testing Into Every AI Collaboration Workflow
improvements.description: Make iterative testing an automatic first step in your process, regardless of task type. Before finalizing any AI output, run at least one test cycle: try the output in a realistic scenario, identify what works and what doesn't, and refine accordingly. Document what you learn from each iteration and explicitly use those insights to inform your next request. This disciplined approach will help you build consistency and develop pattern recognition skills that improve all your future collaborations.
